newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end flat, Jinro group shares higher.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end flat, Jinro group shares higher.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed Tuesday a fraction lower as moves to profit from recent rises contrasted with expected foreign fund inflows, brokers said.
A bailout package by banks helped Jinro Group shares remain strong throughout the day, they said.
But the market shrugged off a slew of economic indicators.
The composite stock index shed 0.11 of a point to 704.05.
"Advanced buying by domestic institutional investors ahead of an expansion in the foreign stock holding limit seemed to end," said Lee Kyung-hoon of Ssangyong Securities.
The foreign share limit of Korean stocks will be raised to 23 percent on Friday from 20 percent at present.
Brokers said investors differed in their views of the market direction after the ceiling expansion.
"Foreign investors are not much excited with the limit rise," said Casey Choe of Union Bank of Switzerland. "I expect the market will stage a consolidation after Friday."

Choe said foreign demand would selectively focus on a handful of core blue chips. But blue chips faced profit-taking on Tuesday. POSCO shed 1,000 won to 54,100 and Samsung Electronics 64050.SK lost 400 won to 61,100.
The weakness of the yen against the dollar and rising short-term interest rates also dented the market, brokers said.
The 80.4 billion won rescue package to the cash-strapped Jinro Group contributed to boosting three listed affiliates of Jinro, the nation's 19st largest conglomerate.
Jinro Ltd rose 510 won to 8,400. Both Jinro General Foods and Jinro Industries went limit up to 4,660 won and 4,900 won respectively.
"The impact of the emergency loans will be short-lived," Lee said. "The amount was far short of Jinro's demand."

Brokers said processing the loans would take time as the Jinro group chairman appeared reluctant to comply with creditors' demand that he issue a letter authorising banks to dispose of his family's shares in group affiliates.
Investors widely ignored signs of an improving economy in indicators released on Tuesday.
Industrial output in March rose 9.1 percent year-on-year, up from a 5.8 percent rise a year earlier.
The current account deficit widened to $2.27 billion in March from $940.2 million a year earlier, but narrowed from February's $2.50 billion deficit.
Inflation, gauged on the consumer price index, rose 4.3 percent in April on the year, down from a 4.6 percent rise a year earlier.
"It's better than our expectations and signals the bottom of the economy may be reached earlier than predicted," said Lee Youn-ho, president of LG Economic Research Institute.
But Choe said: "It's not a big improvement. Investors believe an economic turnaround will take time."
Ssangyong Motors went limit up to 5,740 won on market talk the Ssangyong Group would restructure its business, which was denied by a group spokesman.
